notes.provider: who serves the model: huggingface (HF_TOKEN in .env) or openrouter (OPENROUTER_API_KEY in .env); the model asked is models[provider]
notes.models.huggingface: the Hugging Face model id the agent asks (was VLM_MODEL in .env, then limit vlm_model); the suffix pins one of the router's providers. Pinned to baseten 2026-10-21: the only one that served the agent's request (json_schema + reasoning_effort + image, about 1 s); novita refuses json_schema and, unnamed, reasoning_effort; together needs pay-as-you-go; fireworks-ai, featherless-ai and deepinfra do not serve it. Qwen/Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct is the verified fast fallback
notes.models.openrouter: the OpenRouter model id the agent asks: deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017, the same model as models.huggingface (2026-10-29: back from openai/gpt-6-luna 1/5 and gpt-6.1-sol 0/5 on point_at_the_laptop, both 3-5 false dones; DeepSeek on Baseten was 4/5)
notes.routing: OpenRouter only: its provider preferences, sent as the request's provider object. {} since 2026-10-29 (the user's choice): any host that takes tool calls, OpenRouter picking by price and availability, possibly a different host per request and 4-bit ones (B4 went mostly to Wafer, mxfp4). Pinned to Baseten ({"order": ["baseten"], "allow_fallbacks": false}), B6 scored 3/4 with tool calls. A filter such as {"quantizations": ["fp8", "bf16"]} keeps the 4-bit hosts out. Do not add require_parameters: it drops Baseten (it does not list every parameter sent)
notes.reasoning_effort: one of none, minimal, low, medium, high, default; sent as reasoning_effort. medium on 2026-10-29 for the bench B7 (medium) / B8 (high) on OpenRouter, any host, tool calls, 30 decisions: looking for 5/5 on point_at_the_laptop. B4 (high, before tool calls) did not clearly help. Dropped if the server rejects it
notes.max_tokens: tokens; reply budget, reasoning included; 400 cut a reasoning model off before it answered (a decision used 446), the longest decision seen used 10468 (52 s), and the HF router refused 500000 (its ceiling was 393216). A runaway now ends as a cut-off reply, not a 60 s timeout
notes.temperature: sampling temperature of every model request (0: the most likely reply)
notes.agent.max_decisions: count; model decisions per run, rejected replies included (gpt-policy uses 100) (a limit until 2026-10-29)
notes.agent.step_timeout_s: s; longest wait for one decision before the run fails. 120 since 2026-10-29 (was 60) so a long think at reasoning_effort high is not counted as a failure
notes.agent.request_timeout_s: s; longest one HTTP request to the model may take. 110 since 2026-10-29 (was 30), under step_timeout_s, for reasoning_effort high
notes.agent.retry_max: count; retries when the model is overloaded (a limit until 2026-10-29)
notes.agent.retry_delay_base_s: s; first retry delay; doubles each time (a limit until 2026-10-29)
notes.agent.retry_delay_cap_s: s; largest retry delay (a limit until 2026-10-29)
notes.agent.retry_jitter_s: s; up to this much random time is added to each retry delay (a limit until 2026-10-29)
notes.agent.recovery_timeout_s: s; total time allowed for retries before the run fails (a limit until 2026-10-29)
notes.agent.image_width_px: px; frames are downscaled to this width before they are sent (a limit until 2026-10-29)
notes.agent.jpeg_quality: 0-100; JPEG quality of frames sent to the model (records stay lossless PNG) (a limit until 2026-10-29)
notes.agent.live_image_window: count; observation images kept in the conversation; older turns keep their text (a limit until 2026-10-29)
notes.agent.history_full_turns: count; earlier turns sent in full (observation, image if still in live_image_window, reply); older ones are replaced by one host-written line each, as GPT-Policy's Claude adapter does (a limit until 2026-10-29)
